title: "Variational Autoencoder (VAE)"
description: "A generative model that learns a probability distribution over a compressed latent representation."
term: "Variational Autoencoder (VAE)"
letter: "V"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Advanced"

## Simple explanation

A variational autoencoder learns to compress examples into a space where
nearby points represent related data, then decode points from that space into
plausible examples. Unlike an ordinary autoencoder, it learns a distribution
so new points can be sampled.

## Technical explanation

An encoder predicts parameters of a latent distribution, commonly a Gaussian
with mean $\mu(x)$ and diagonal variance $\sigma^2(x)$. A latent vector is
sampled using the reparameterization trick,
$z=\mu(x)+\sigma(x)\odot\epsilon$ for $\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)$, allowing
gradient-based training. The decoder models $p_\theta(x\mid z)$. The objective
maximizes a variational lower bound, balancing reconstruction likelihood and a
regularizing divergence from a prior such as $\mathcal{N}(0,I)$.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

VAEs provide a principled way to learn generative latent spaces for synthesis,
representation learning, and anomaly detection. Their explicit latent
distribution also enables interpolation and controlled sampling, though
reconstruction quality and sample fidelity can trade off.

## How it works

The encoder maps each input to distribution parameters. Training samples a
latent point and decodes it; the loss rewards accurate reconstruction while
keeping the encoded distribution near the prior. At generation time, sample
$z$ from the prior and pass it through the decoder.

The reconstruction objective depends on the data type: for example, a
Bernoulli likelihood for binary pixels or a Gaussian likelihood for continuous
values. It should reflect the intended observation model rather than being
chosen only for convenience.

## Practical example

Train a VAE on images of handwritten digits. To generate a new image, sample a
latent vector from the learned prior and decode it; moving between two latent
vectors can produce a smooth visual interpolation.

## Common misconceptions

- A VAE is not simply an autoencoder with random noise added; its probabilistic
  objective and learned latent distribution are central.
- A smooth latent space does not guarantee every sampled point decodes to a
  high-quality example.
